description:
Somos un equipo de seis integrantes apasionados por la ciencia, la tecnología y la innovación. Nos interesa desarrollar soluciones creativas a problemas reales mediante el trabajo colaborativo, el pensamiento crítico y la aplicación de conocimientos científicos.

Buscamos personas comprometidas, creativas, con iniciativa y ganas de aprender, que aporten habilidades en programación, diseño, investigación, química y resolución de problemas.
summary: Vesperium Rescate Estelar is an interactive web game that allows children and young people to virtually travel to space to discover the legacy of historic NASA missions. The project addresses the challenge of giving a voice to the equipment humanity has left behind on other worlds. Upon entering, the player chooses between the Moon or Mars to display key information about each location. On the planet, they control a small robot that collects scattered pieces; upon assembling each historical artifact, the game narrates its original mission and achievements. This project is important because it brings children closer to such distant and unreachable worlds through a tangible experience, transforming spatial distance and scientific data into an accessible adventure that sparks their imagination and scientific vocation from an early age. In this way, we inspire new generations to connect with space history through play.
details:
Vesperium is an interactive web video game developed with an educational and science communication focus, designed to inspire new generations through the history of space exploration.
The project consists of an experience where the user controls a small scavenger robot whose mission is to explore the surface of the Moon and Mars to rescue abandoned pieces of historical hardware. Upon collecting each artifact such as the ALSEP instruments and lunar rovers on the Moon, missions on Mars, and the Kepler space telescope the game displays interactive cards that reveal their true identity, the purpose of their engineering design, and the scientific impact of their discoveries for humanity.
The system operates through a fluid web interface where the player navigates planetary environments and interacts with visual elements through simple collection mechanics. Upon approaching a metallic piece, a modular component in the form of an informational card is activated, detailing the technical and scientific history of the NASA mission in an educational and accessible way for all audiences.
The primary impact of Vesperium is to transform the perception of "space debris" into a living archive of knowledge. Its goal is to educate, foster interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM), and rescue from oblivion the technological milestones that built our current understanding of the cosmos.
For the development and implementation of the project, our team used HTML and CSS to structure and style the web interface, ensuring that the game is lightweight, responsive, and accessible from any browser without requiring heavy installations. For the graphic design, we used Piskel, which allowed us to design and animate from scratch in a pixel art style both our scavenger robot and the sprites of the space artifacts and planetary scenarios.
Vesperium stands out for its originality by fusing a retro pixel art aesthetic and playful narrative with rigorous scientific content based on official archives from space missions. Our team prioritized user experience (UX), ensuring that the transition between visual exploration and educational reading was organic, intuitive, and engaging for younger players.
